newsitem.title: USA: U.S. firm on expanding NATO as summit nears.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firm on expanding NATO as summit nears.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, speaking two days before the Helsinki U.S.-Russia summit, said on Tuesday NATO expansion would go ahead despite Russian objections.

"NATO enlargement will remain on track. New allies will enjoy the full benefits and assume the full responsibilities of membership. The first new members will not be the last and we will exclude no European democracy from future consideration," Albright told reporters.

Albright will be accompanying President Bill Clinton to the Finnish capital for the meetings with President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday and Friday. She held intensive talks over the last few days in Washington with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.

She said Washington was determined to protect the interests of the central European countries. "I can assure you that neither the president nor I are going to bargain away the rights of the Central Europeans. Neither justice nor history will allow that." She said in discussions on Europe's future, Russia would "have a seat at the table" but not a veto. Poland, the Czech Reopublic and Hungary are expected to be among the former Soviet-allied countries to be offered NATO membership.

On a charter being negotiated between Russia and NATO to set out a course for future relations between them, Albright said: "The point of the charter is to advance an enduring interest NATO and Russia will continue to share ... for this reason, while we would welcome agreement in the next few months, there is no deadline, not in Helsinki or in (the July NATO summit in) Madrid. The door will stay open."

She stressed that this was a time for cooperation, not confrontation with Russia. "We do not face a choice between diminishing NATO or diminishing Russia. It is not 1949 or 1989 (which marked the effective start and end of the Cold War). Today we are all on the same side ..."
